raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #48336.

GLM-5.3-Flash's chat template ignores the `enable_thinking` kwarg and always ends the rendered prompt with the think-start token (depth is controlled by `reasoning_effort`). The glm47 full-assistant EBNF derived its thinking state from the raw kwarg: with `enable_thinking=False` and `accommodate_chat_template=True`, `generate_glm_grammar` emitted `thinking_block ::= ""` and excluded the think-end token everywhere else. A model already inside the template-opened thinking block could never close it, so **every** request with `tools` + `enable_thinking: false` ran to `max_tokens` with `finish_reason: "length"`, empty `content` and no tool call — even a trivial one. Without tools no grammar is built and the same request is fine; with `enable_thinking: true` or the kwarg omitted, also fine. Clients and gateways commonly send `enable_thinking: false` (the Qwen3-style convention), turning it into a guaranteed runaway generation against this model.

## Modifications

One branch of `generate_glm_grammar` (`glm4_moe_detector.py`): the glm47, `enable_thinking=False`, `accommodate_chat_template=True` case now emits

```ebnf
thinking_block ::= ( thinking_block_content "<think-end>" )?
```

instead of `thinking_block ::= ""`. This is correct for both template styles:

- **templates that honor `enable_thinking`** render no think-start; the optional block is skipped and the model still goes straight to the answer or a tool call — the grammar still allows exactly what it allowed before, minus the trap;
- **templates that ignore the kwarg** (GLM-5.3-Flash) open the thinking block themselves; the model can now close it and proceed normally.

The `thinking=True` shapes are untouched, and the glm45 branch is left unchanged (it has no runtime caller — the only call site hardcodes `chat_template_version="glm47"`).

The trade-off is that `enable_thinking=False` no longer *bans* a thinking block from the grammar; it still means "tell the template not to think", and for templates that honor it nothing changes in practice. Banning the close token, however, is what turned an ignored kwarg into a hang.

## Regression Tests

New `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_glm47_grammar_thinking.py` compiles the generated EBNF with xgrammar and asserts string acceptance:

- the regression case: `"<think-end>391"` is accepted with `enable_thinking=False` (the template already opened the block; the very first generated token may be the close token) — **fails on the pre-fix grammar**;
- `"<think-end><tool-call…>"` likewise accepted — **fails on the pre-fix grammar**;
- direct answer / direct tool call still accepted with `enable_thinking=False` (templates that honor the kwarg keep working);
- `thinking=True` still rejects an answer without a preceding think-end and accepts the closed one; the non-accommodate full-block form still accepts `<think-start>…<think-end>answer`.

Also verified with a minimal tokenizer that the fixed grammar's first-token allow-set contains the think-end token (it was absent before the fix) while the tool-call and plain-text alternatives are unchanged.

## Test Results

- New suite: 6/6 with the fix; stashing the fix keeps exactly the 2 regression cases red.
- Full `test/registered/unit/function_call/` sweep: 651 passed, 17 failed — all pre-existing on a clean tree (same failure list with the fix stashed; local structural-tag env issues also present when #45962 landed).
- `test_serving_chat.py`: 172 passed, 1 pre-existing failure (`test_streaming_created_is_stable_across_chunks`, missing `tml-renderers` package in this offline env).
- `ruff check --select=F401,F821,F823,UP037`, `ruff format`, `isort` (7.0.0, matching pre-commit): clean.

## Checklist

- [x] I have referenced the issue fixed (#48336).
- [x] I have created at least one test case for the fix.

@@ -0,0 +1,104 @@
+"""glm47 full-assistant EBNF: the grammar's thinking state must survive
+chat templates that ignore ``enable_thinking``.
+
+GLM-5.3-Flash's chat template ignores the ``enable_thinking`` kwarg and
+always ends the rendered prompt with the think-start token. The glm47
+grammar used to derive its thinking state from the raw kwarg: with
+``enable_thinking=False`` it emitted ``thinking_block ::= ""`` and excluded
+the think-end token everywhere else, so a model already inside a template-
+opened thinking block could never close it and generated until
+``max_tokens`` with empty content and no tool call (issue #48336). The
+grammar now allows an optional, possibly empty thinking block, which is
+correct for both template styles.
+"""
+
+import xgrammar as xgr
+from xgrammar.testing import _is_grammar_accept_string
+
+from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function
+from sglang.srt.function_call.glm4_moe_detector import (
+    GlmSpecialTokenConfig,
+    generate_glm_grammar,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+T = GlmSpecialTokenConfig()
+
+_FUNCS = [
+    Function(
+        name="shell",
+        description="run a shell command",
+        parameters={
+            "type": "object",
+            "properties": {"cmd": {"type": "string"}},
+            "required": ["cmd"],
+        },
+    )
+]
+
+THINK_CLOSE_THEN_ANSWER = f"{T.end_of_thinking}391"
+TOOL_CALL = (
+    f"{T.begin_of_tool_call}shell"
+    f"{T.begin_of_key}cmd{T.end_of_key}"
+    f"{T.begin_of_value}ls{T.end_of_value}"
+    f"{T.end_of_tool_call}"
+)
+
+
+def _grammar(enable_thinking, accommodate=True):
+    ebnf = generate_glm_grammar(
+        enable_thinking=enable_thinking,
+        functions=_FUNCS,
+        special_tokens=T,
+        chat_template_version="glm47",
+        accommodate_chat_template=accommodate,
+        allow_multiple_assistant_turns=False,
+    )
+    return xgr.Grammar.from_ebnf(ebnf)
+
+
+def _accepts(grammar, text):
+    return _is_grammar_accept_string(grammar, text)
+
+
+class TestGlm47GrammarThinkingState(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_thinking_false_allows_closing_a_template_opened_think_block(self):
+        """Regression for #48336: the template ignored enable_thinking and
+        already opened the thinking block, so the very first generated token
+        may be the think-end token. Banning it traps the model until
+        max_tokens."""
+        self.assertTrue(_accepts(_grammar(False), THINK_CLOSE_THEN_ANSWER))
+
+    def test_thinking_false_still_allows_direct_answer(self):
+        """Templates that honor enable_thinking render no think-start; the
+        model goes straight to the answer."""
+        self.assertTrue(_accepts(_grammar(False), "391"))
+
+    def test_thinking_false_still_allows_direct_tool_call(self):
+        self.assertTrue(_accepts(_grammar(False), TOOL_CALL))
+
+    def test_thinking_false_allows_think_close_then_tool_call(self):
+        self.assertTrue(_accepts(_grammar(False), f"{T.end_of_thinking}{TOOL_CALL}"))
+
+    def test_thinking_true_still_requires_thinking_first(self):
+        grammar = _grammar(True)
+        self.assertFalse(_accepts(grammar, "391"))
+        self.assertTrue(_accepts(grammar, THINK_CLOSE_THEN_ANSWER))
+
+    def test_thinking_true_non_accommodate_accepts_full_block(self):
+        grammar = _grammar(True, accommodate=False)
+        self.assertTrue(
+            _accepts(
+                grammar,
+                f"{T.begin_of_thinking}why{T.end_of_thinking}391",
+            )
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    import unittest
+
+    unittest.main()
